sources.quote: Kashyapa moved the capital and his residence from the traditional capital of Anuradhapura to the more secure summit of Sigiriya.

sources.quote: The gardens are divided into three distinct but linked forms: water gardens, cave and boulder gardens, and terraced gardens.
It is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning.

facts.rationale: Wikipedia lists water, boulder and terraced gardens, moats/walls, and calls it one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning.

sources.quote: a granite peak standing some 180m high (the 'Lion's Rock', which dominates the jungle from all sides)
dominated by a massive column of granite approximately 180 m

facts.rationale: UNESCO and Wikipedia give ~180 m; 200 m is ~11% off, beyond tolerance. Rock is a granite magma plug (not strictly 'volcanic rock'). Matale District/Central Province is correct.

sources.quote: Most of the elaborate constructions on the rock summit and around it, including defensive structures, palaces, and gardens, date from this period.

facts.rationale: Palaces, gardens, defensive structures and a man-made reservoir are documented.

sources.quote: covered in highly polished white plaster, the wall is now partially covered with verses scribbled by visitors, some of them dating from as early as the 8th century.
Medieval Sinhalese, which emerged around 750 AD, is thought to be derived from Grantha script.

facts.rationale: Resolved: A unverifiable, B contradicted/overstated. Deciding source Wikipedia Sinhala_script: the script's infobox time period is '8th century CE - present' and Medieval Sinhalese emerged c. 750 AD (earlier Brahmi-stage inscriptions are described as a break), so 8th-century mirror-wall verses (Wikipedia Sigiriya) do rank among the oldest Sinhala-script examples; B's 3rd-century-BCE Brahmi ancestry does not contradict that.
